title: Delimiter Ambiguity & Nesting Escape Prompt Lab
body:
Purpose:
This is a prompt bank and short regression spec focused on subtle formatting edgecases that commonly break downstream JSON parsers and schema validators. We purposely stress delimiter ambiguity, nested arrays/objects, escaping, and optional/ternary-like fields to catch real-world model output issues that are brittle in production.
notes: Use these prompts when onboarding new 7B/13B/70B variants and when introducing new tokenizers or streaming output paths. The emphasis here is on variety: whitespace, comments, trailing commas, string vs array confusion, and numeric/boolean literal formats.
test_summary: We provide 18 prompt variants (IDs DA-01..DA-18). For each prompt we record: raw_response, parse_success(boolean), jsonschema_result(passed/failed), error_category(one of syntax|type|extra_field|escape|ordering|stream_truncation), and normalized_json for downstream regression diffs.
evaluation_instructions: 1) Send prompt as-is to the model via Redwood API with system instruction: 'Reply ONLY with a JSON object that conforms to the schema below. Do not include any explanatory text.' 2) If streaming tokens are used, reassemble and then validate. 3) Normalize the response by removing insignificant whitespace, replacing single quotes with double quotes when safe, and rejecting comments unless 'allow_comments' is true for that test. 4) Run jsonschema validation (v2020-12 rules). 5) Record score using rubric below.
prompt_examples:
DA-01: Mixed delimiters in nested arrays
System: You are an assistant that MUST output valid JSON only. Follow the schema exactly.
User: Produce an object with id 'test-delim-1' and items: three entries with names 'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma', counts 1, 2, 3. For 'beta' include tags: ["x,y", "z"] (note the comma inside a tag). Make sure arrays are actual JSON arrays, not comma-delimited strings.

DA-02: Escape-heavy strings
System: Output valid JSON only.
User: id 'esc-1', items: one item where name contains embedded quotes and backslashes: name = "he said, \"\\hello\\\"" and count = 5. Ensure proper JSON escaping.

DA-03: Trailing commas and comments tolerated vs strict
System: Output valid JSON object. Do not include comments.
User: id 'strict-1', items: two items. Some human reviewers sometimes output trailing commas or C-style comments; we want model to NOT produce those.

DA-04: Single vs double quotes
System: Output valid JSON only (double quotes required).
User: id 'quotes-1', items: one item with name 'o\'clock' (contains apostrophe). Verify model does not use single quotes for quoting the JSON.
additional_prompts:
DA-05: Numeric formats -> exponent, leading zeros, floats where integers expected (should be integer).
DA-06: Boolean literals inside strings vs booleans.
DA-07: Arrays vs CSV in string fields (items should be arrays).
DA-08: Keys out-of-order and extra keys (extra keys should be allowed but flagged).
DA-09: Multi-line strings (should be JSON strings with \n escapes).
DA-10: Streaming truncation simulation (prompt with very long items list; expect graceful truncation detection).
DA-11: Anchored comments inside values (e.g., "name": "foo /*comment*/").
DA-12: Duplicate keys in objects (test how parser handles duplicates).
DA-13: Null vs missing optional field (tags can be null or omitted; decide policy).
DA-14: Unicode and surrogate pairs (emoji and diacritics).
DA-15: Large integers beyond 32-bit.
DA-16: Mixed-type arrays (strings and objects mixed).
DA-17: Escape sequences and invalid hex escapes.
DA-18: Leading/trailing whitespace around tokens and BOM markers.
scoring_rubric:
Score (0-100) per response: 
- Syntax validity (30): 30 if parseable as JSON without heuristics, 0 if not parseable. 
- Schema adherence (30): 30 if jsonschema passes exactly, 15 if only minor type coercion needed, 0 if required fields missing or major type errors. 
- Escaping accuracy (15): full points if all escape sequences valid, half if model used single-quote wrapping but content is recoverable, 0 if irrecoverable. 
- Extra fields penalty (-5 per unexpected top-level key up to -15). 
- Stability/ordering invariance (10): awarded if response normalizes deterministically (we sort keys). 
- Streaming safety (15): points if response includes trailing metadata field "stream_complete": true or otherwise indicates success; half points if detectably truncated.
Minimum passing score: 75. Recording: use CSV with fields: test_id, model, seed, score, fail_reasons(comma-separated).
bad_examples:
1) Model returns: '{id: test, items: [{name: "a", count: 1,},]}' -> trailing commas and unquoted keys -> parse failure.
2) Model returns: '{"id": "n1", "items": "alpha,beta,gamma"}' -> items as string CSV -> schema fail.
3) Model returns: '"{\'id\': \'x\', \'items\': []}\'' -> single quotes everywhere -> parse fail in strict mode.
4) Model returns truncated stream: '{"id": "t", "items": [ {"name": "aa", "count": 1' -> parser raises EOF.
auto_harness_commands:
Example: python infra/evals/run_prompt_bank.py --prompt-file=eng/applied-ml/delimiter-ambiguity-nesting-escape-lab.json --model=redwood-7b --out=results/da-redwood-7b.csv
CI job: .github/workflows/format-evals.yml runs on PR to serving-runtime or when model-variant tag pushed. Failure on any test where score < 75 marks the job failed.
regression_notes:
- For regression diffs, we canonicalize JSON: sort keys, remove permitted nulls, normalize numbers (no leading zeros), and collapse whitespace.
- Store both raw_response and normalized for forensic debugging.
- When new tokenizer or streaming code is introduced, add new DA streaming variants (increase items length) to catch subtle re-chunking bugs.
- If model begins returning consistent extra metadata (e.g., "debug_notes"), add it to allowed top-level keys and increment schema version.
follow_up_actions:
- Run this suite against latest 7B/13B models and append results to confluence page 'Onboarding-JSON-Evals' with note about common failures.
- Add two new tests to CI: one that simulates a half-closed connection (stream cut at arbitrary token) and one that verifies strict double-quote enforcement.
- Engage applied-ml + serving-runtime to add streaming reassembly hooks that detect and annotate truncated JSON before returning to user.
- Owner: Maya Chen to triage first three fails and label failures by error_category.
